taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Court-road, Bori Metropolis. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 16.8 | 2.56 | 2.56
2 | 73.3 | 10.4 | 12.9
3 | 701 | 49.9 | 62.9
4 | 51.6 | 51.4 | 114
5 | 99.8 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as AKH-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Court-road, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report — Station Court-road, Bori Metropolis**

The VES interpretation at Court-road reveals a five-layer subsurface sequence. Resistivity increases from Layer 1 (16.8 Ω·m) through Layer 2 (73.3 Ω·m) to a resistive Layer 3 (701 Ω·m), likely representing a competent or dry formation. This is underlain by a lower-resistivity Layer 4 (51.6 Ω·m), interpreted as a more conductive zone (possibly saturated or clay-rich), before resistivity rises again in Layer 5 (99.8 Ω·m).

Applying the standard curve-type convention to the resistivity sequence (16.8–73.3–701–51.6–99.8):

- Layers 1-2-3: increasing → A
- Layers 2-3-4: rise then fall → K
- Layers 3-4-5: fall then rise → H

This yields a curve type of **AKH**, consistent with the classification on file. No discrepancy was found between the computed curve type and the filed interpretation.

{"curve_type_stated": "AKH", "label_issue_flagged": false}
